external_page_requires.interface: The published autonomous Euler theorem proves root-mean-square order one-half under its uniform all-finite-moment and coefficient hypotheses. It does not prove a Milstein order-one estimate and is not used as a premise for the local Milstein proof.

The multidimensional Ito formula is used on the exact SDE solution and its coefficient functions; the local estimates use the square-integrable Ito isometry and martingale increment property. The cited Ito and Brownian interfaces assume AC and the standing usual-filtration/integrability conventions, which the authored results state.

The hierarchy definition supplies dyadic level corrections and shared couplings; the complexity theorem requires alpha at least one-half, a correction variance rate beta greater than zero, and per-sample work O(h^-1). T13 proves alpha=1, beta=2, and the work bound locally before applying it.
